kurz: Heat travels slowly from the outside in. That is why the edge is long done while the centre is still cold.
bild_im_kopf: Like a message whispered along a human chain: it takes a while to reach the middle.
was_passiert: In food, each particle passes the heat on to its neighbours. That is slow: pieces twice as thick take roughly four times as long for the centre to get warm. The hotter the outside, the bigger the difference between edge and centre.
warum_wichtig: Explains grey edges on steaks, raw centres in thick roasts and why [[rueckwaerts-garen|reverse searing]] works.
faustregeln: Cook thick pieces gently, thin ones hot and fast.
Halving the thickness roughly quarters the cooking time (as a guide).

stellschrauben.wirkung: cast iron stores heat, aluminium conducts it fast
